meta.title: Raoul Pal: Brutally Honest Advice About Crypto Investing (that nobody wants to hear)
meta.thread_line: 3 threads · responsibility for copy-traders · expect 50% drawdowns · the few layer-ones that matter

snapshot: Short clip: the host asks Pal about the 2025 statement that he was over **70%** in Sui and whether he still stands by it.
Pal still holds the position, but won't discuss sizing, saying people copy a trade without doing the work or having his income and risk tolerance.
He feels responsible for followers who bought later, and tells them to add into weakness so entry price stops mattering.
He tells newcomers to assume a **50%** drawdown: Bitcoin 35% pullbacks, 70% further down the risk curve, and Solana and Ethereum both fell 70-80% mid-bull before multiplying.
Thesis: three to five layer-one chains become systemically important and capture 80% of block space; outside Solana and Ethereum, he sees only Sui.
Real Vision plans to build copy trading in, aiming for thesis-level discussion rather than blind copying.

themes.title: Why Pal won't give position sizes and still feels responsible
themes.lead: Pal says his Sui weighting was his choice given his income and risk, and that copying a trade without the thesis is what hurts people.
bullets: The host recalls Pal saying on an earlier episode that he was massively overweight Sui at more than **70%**; Pal now says he can't tell people percentages because they copy without doing the work.
He cites income, industry knowledge and risk tolerance as why his sizing doesn't transfer: if it fails he is 'still absolutely fine'.
Followers who bought much later feel burned; Pal says he feels responsible, that his thesis is yet to be proven and needs a full up cycle first.
His fix: add into weakness. Buying at 70, 75, 80 cents lowers the average entry, so the original entry level matters less over time.
He says he published a 'don't mess this up' thesis, even NFTs and t-shirts of it, but people bought the high anyway; he adds that he isn't telling anyone to buy.
The host says that since Celsius and FTX he doesn't advise anyone to buy crypto; Pal answers with 'here's what I'm doing, but I don't think you should do it'.
themes.watch: Pal co-founded Real Vision, which is building copy trading in, and he holds the position he discusses.

names.name: Sui (SUI)
names.blurb: Pal's large position; still comfortable but won't discuss sizing

themes.title: Assume you will be down 50% at some point
themes.lead: Newcomers should accept that the day they buy is rarely the low and that large drawdowns happen even in winning trades.
bullets: Host: newcomers will probably be down at least **50%** at some point, and each new position probably will be too, even if it rises first.
Pal: nobody knows when it comes, today or in a year; his 'don't mess this up' thesis said to expect 35% pullbacks in Bitcoin alone, and about 70% further down the risk curve.
History: Solana fell 80% in 2020 mid-bull run, and Ethereum did the same in 2017; these fell 50-70% and still ended up around 50x.

names.name: Ethereum (ETH)
names.blurb: Fell similarly in 2017 and ended up 50x

themes.title: Three to five layer-ones will capture 80% of block space
themes.lead: Pal sees very few layer-ones with adoption and a technology stack different from Solana or Ethereum, and Sui is the only one he sees joining the top three.
bullets: Thesis: three to five layer-ones become systemically important and capture 80% of the entire market for block space.
He sees no other chain besides Sui that can get into the top three, alongside Solana and Ethereum.
NEAR is built for a different purpose; Avalanche is a possibility he can see.
Because so few qualify, he thinks you can build a basket and assume a couple don't work out.

quote.text: I don't see another one outside of Sui that can get into the top three.

themes.watch: Pal holds Sui and co-founded Real Vision, which publishes crypto research.

takeaways.title: Size positions to your own income and risk tolerance, never to someone else's disclosed percentage.
Pre-plan for a 50% drawdown before entering any new crypto position.
If you hold a thesis through weakness, add rather than cut to improve your average entry.
Test the layer-one thesis by asking which chain has real adoption and a different technology stack.

hot_takes.take: I do believe there'll be three to five layer ones that are systemically important and they will capture 80% of the entire market for block space.
I don't see another one outside of Sui that can get into the top three.

claims.claim: Three to five layer-one chains will capture 80% of the market for block space.
Sui is the only layer-one besides Solana and Ethereum that can reach the top three.
Expect 35% pullbacks in Bitcoin and around 70% further out the risk curve.

glossary.def: The capacity of a blockchain to process transactions, which layer-ones compete to sell.
A base blockchain such as Ethereum, Solana or Sui, as opposed to apps or networks built on top.
Mirroring another investor's trades, entry and size without doing your own analysis.
